speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To begin assessing the infant's feeding difficulties and abdominal distension, could you describe his typical stool consistency and frequency? Additionally, has there been any visible blood or mucus in the diapers?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: The infant's fussiness and abdominal tenderness are concerning, so I need to know if he has had any vomiting, and if so, is it bilious (green) or non-bilious? Has he passed any stool recently, and if so, what was its appearance?

speaker: Patient
text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications.

speaker: Doctor
text: He has not had vomiting or diarrhea, which makes an infectious gastroenteritis less likely. Has he passed any stool since birth, and if so, was there any delay in the passage of meconium in the first 48 hours of life?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby did not seem to pass stool normally and the belly swelling has become more obvious. Feeding has clearly decreased over the past few days.

speaker: Doctor
text: The delayed stool passage and progressive abdominal distension are highly suggestive of a lower intestinal obstruction like Hirschsprung disease. I will request an abdominal X-ray to check for dilated bowel loops and air-fluid levels, and I need to know if a rectal exam elicited an explosive release of gas or stool?
